findings.title: Call to non-existent no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added to its superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no no-argument overload in UsernamePasswordForm or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this code does not compile and blocks building the services module and running any of the added tests.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys now disabled for unidentified users, breaking initial discoverable login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requires user != null, and it is used in authenticate() and in challenge(context, error, field). Previously conditional WebAuthn data was filled when no user had been identified, which is the normal first-login case for discoverable passkeys: the credential itself supplies the user. With the new predicate, opening the username/password page initially (context.getUser() == null) never calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(), so no challenge/RP data or conditional-UI form is rendered and automatic passkey login cannot happen; the same loss occurs after an invalid-username challenge where the user is null. The predicate should enable passkeys based on the realm/feature setting regardless of whether a user is already identified, while only restricting the listed authenticators for an identified user.
